title: Why do I have problems with color numbers?

posts.author: Tangram
posts.body: Hi everyone, I'm brand new to the community and I recently started using RPG Maker MV and I'm taking my first steps. I'm trying to write a text in red with the code /C[1], the 1 should be the number of red however it gives me the color cyan, I have no active plugins other than the first basic one, do you know how to solve the problem?

posts.author: MissCircle
posts.body: /C[1] gives cyan and /C[18] gives red as seen in file which I pinned. If im wrong correct me

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body: It starts counting with 0, that might be the issue.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Tangram said:
I'm trying to write a text in red with the code /C[1], the 1 should be the number of red
Click to expand...
I guess the question is: why do you think so?
According to the blocks in the Window.png file (zoomed in and labeled above), red is nowhere near 1.
Even if you were looking at the orange block on the top row and calling that red, it's the third block in.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
all of that above actually depends on the windowskin used.
the counting starts with zero, but the effect is actually "the color in the square responding to the number used", so if you change the windowskin then you'll change the color reference.
Since 1 is by default nowhere near red, the OP might have gotten the reference from a game where the windowskin was changed.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Their graphic might help you, as those are the default colors used in most window skins. But if you use a skin with a different palette, the numbers won't match.
When you right click your "Show Text" message box and select "insert color index", you can see your palette and click the color you want to get the right number.
